chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: How hostesses and tickets worked at big ballrooms
summary: At big ballrooms patrons paid admission and bought tickets for hostesses, and bands alternated half-hour sets.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: And there what was the setup? An admission?
Well, they had girls, too -- hostesses. The big-time ballrooms, they had hostesses. You know, like the Savoy, the Roseland -- they had hostesses. And the Arcadia, yeah.
But it wasn't... In other words, people paid to get in, and they didn't pay for...
They paid to get in, and then they paid to dance with the hostesses. So you go in, you pay your money
to get in -- now you have nobody to dance with. So yo go to the hostess and you buy a ticket. She'll dance with you -- until your ticket's run out.
There it was one ticket for at least a whole number, right, rather than just a chorus.

Well, yeah. The band didn't stop after one chorus. The band played their numbers, whatever, how they had them... Of course, I don't know how the hostesses did with the tickets. I guess they charged more for the tickets, maybe. I didn't talk to none of them, so I didn't know.
But that kind of job must have been pretty good, because you must have gotten a rest when the other bands went on.
Oh yeah, yeah! I mean, that was just like the work now. We'd work a half-hour on, a half-hour off, and the other band would play. You know...
